items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: he would play, the older Fats Navarro and Howard McGhee and of course Bird and Monk and all those people. So I found myself walking to my violin lesson whistling “Groovin’ High” and “Scrapple from the Apple.”

ctx.x: But I started, what six years old, I guess it was the start of the first grade, but when I was in high school, about the eleventh grade there used to be a DJ out here named Gene Norman, who has since become a record producer, and he had a show called “The East Side Show” and it was all jazz. And of course that’s the time that — the coast has always been big with Stan Kenton and Woody Herman because they were out here a lot of the time. But in addition to hearing that, Shorty had left Stan’s band and so I heard…
Did you have any aspirations of being a professional musician as a senior in high school?
